subject: Dedicated capacity handoff & temporary SLO contraction — proposed runbook
messages:
From: Tim Parsons <tim@aurora-networks.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Networks Legal <legal@aurora-networks.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — request for a 'handoff' procedure + temporary SLO contraction

Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We are aligned on most terms, but legal and our SREs flagged a gap around scheduled maintenance and an aggressive failover when our reserved GPUs transition to burst or on-demand capacity. Specifically: if you need to pull reserved nodes for maintenance or hardware failover, Aurora needs a predictable handoff window where we accept a temporarily tighter SLO for tail latency (e.g., 99.9 -> 99.5) for up to 30 minutes, and an explicit observable runbook that engineers can follow during the transition.

Can Redwood provide a short playbook we can add to the contract as an appendix and confirm what credits (if any) apply if the handoff goes beyond the agreed window? We are trying to avoid broad carveouts; legal asked for a precise, time-bounded procedure and automatic monitoring hooks so our incident response can be prescriptive.

I attached a sketch of how Aurora's SREs see the handoff (aurora_handoff_sketch_v1.pdf).

Best,
Tim

--
Tim Parsons
Head of Platform Reliability
Aurora Networks
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Tim Parsons <tim@aurora-networks.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — request for a 'handoff' procedure + temporary SLO contraction

Tim —

Thanks for the clear ask and the sketch, much appreciated. We're happy to formalize a handoff playbook. High level proposal:

- Scope: Applies only to planned maintenance and hardware-level failover of reserved pool nodes. Not for arbitrary autoscaling.
- Window: 30 minute standard handoff window where latency SLO (99.9) may be relaxed to 99.5 for affected flows; automatic reversion after window unless extended by mutual written consent.
- Observability: Redwood will emit a dedicated handoff event (+trace id) to the customer's event stream and post a short-term SLO metric to the Console with a preconfigured dashboard link.
- Credits: For excursions beyond the window, we propose a tiered credit: 5% usage credit for the first additional 30 minutes, 10% for the next hour.
- Runbook: we will produce a 1–2 page runbook with exact steps (initiate handoff, signal KV-cache drain, route to burst pool, validate tail latency, revert).

I'll draft the runbook and share as PDF for legal review. Evelyn & Ben — can you take point on the runbook and attach the monitoring hooks we can emit?

Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales (Dedicated Capacity)
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tim Parsons <tim@aurora-networks.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — request for a 'handoff' procedure + temporary SLO contraction

Tim / Jordan / Ben —

Attached is a first draft of the runbook (draft_handoff_runbook.pdf) and a short checklist that the SRE on-call will follow. Key elements included:

1) Pre-handoff checks (traffic trimming, KV cache snapshot)
2) Signal: REDWOOD-HANDOFF-START event (includes cluster-id, affected model/version, expected duration)
3) Drain: KV-cache drain with a 90s soft-drain window and autosplit to burst pool
4) Validation: 1-minute rolling 99th/99.9th checks; automatic rollback if latency > threshold for 3 consecutive minutes
5) Extension path: on-call + Aurora SRE must acknowledge and sign-off (email + Console acknowledgment) to extend beyond 30 minutes
6) Credit calc: automatic ticket creation to billing with evidence link if extension triggered

Notes/asks for Aurora:
- Where would your SRE team like the Console dashboard link posted (team Ops hook vs. global alerts)?
- We propose DocuSign appendix language that references the runbook and the event ids. Legal to legal can iterate on exact wording.

Tim — please review and let us know if the validation thresholds or drain timings need tuning.

Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineering Lead, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
From: Tim Parsons <tim@aurora-networks.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Networks Legal <legal@aurora-networks.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — request for a 'handoff' procedure + temporary SLO contraction

Evelyn / Jordan —

This draft looks good and addresses the ask in a pragmatic way. A few quick items from our SRE team:

- Increase soft-drain window to 120s for our heavier KV payloads.
- Validation: prefer an additional synthetic probe (app-level e2e) before sign-off.
- Credit: legal prefers fixed credit table vs. percentage tiers (e.g., >30–60m = $5k, >60–120m = $12k).

If you can update the runbook with those two technical changes and swap the credit wording to a fixed table we can move to legal review and append to the SOW. Also confirm that there is an automatic Console event that creates the billing ticket if extension is triggered (we need that to avoid manual evidence collection).

If you can get the revised PDF to us by EOD June 2 we can circle back with Legal the following week.

Thanks — we're aligned to proceed once runbook is updated.

Best,
Tim

--
Tim Parsons
Head of Platform Reliability
Aurora Networks
